text:
beth: quick sync — I'm sketching an 'onramp credit bridge' to avoid churn between trial credits and first commit. short ask: validate constraints, launch criteria, and what sales needs to offer to customers.

julio: +1 — customers keep asking for something to cover first-month spikes. they want predictable safety net they can opt into. example: startup needs 2 weeks of extra capacity while they finalize infra.

eng-kai: feasible technically. two parts: (1) issuance & expiry of temporary credits, (2) automatic conversion rules when commit hits. automation is the tricky bit for corner cases (partial conversion, refunds).

finance-nick: concern: revenue recognition + GAAP if we debit credits vs invoice. We need clear guidance on when credits are considered a discount vs deferred revenue. propose expire-without-value model to avoid recognizing as prepaid.

legal-lena: +1 on contract language. must be explicit: "bridge credits are promotional, expire X days, non-transferable". also flag GDPR/data-residency clauses if bridge tied to region-specific pricing.

maria: rollout ops note: must be self-serve in console + sales UI checkbox. telemetry events: {"bridge_offered","bridge_accepted","bridge_consumed","bridge_expired"}. need migration path for existing trials.

oleg: metric side: measure conversion delta (30d/90d), MRR retention lift, and top-10 customers who use bridge. A/B candidate: offer bridge to random 50% of trials for 8 weeks.

design-anya: UX should not look like a discount trap. propose a one-screen modal: "Bridge offer — covers short-term usage spikes for N days. Accept/Decline. See terms." keep opt-in default off, but easy for sales to flip.

julio: sales checklist: clear script + one-pager for customers. SLA impacts? if bridge enables extra throughput, does it change routing priority? we should default to same QoS as trial (no priority lane).

eng-kai: on SLA: bridge should not grant priority-lane or reserved capacity. it's purely credit balance. If they need reserved throughput we escalate to Dedicated pilot.

beth: proposed config (example):
```
bridge:
  duration_days: 30
  cap_percent_of_trial: 50
  opt_in: true
  expiry_action: "revert_to_paid_quota"
  allow_conversion: true
```
This keeps it simple: customers get up to 50% of their trial monthly spend as one-time bridge credits, valid 30 days. opt-in required.

finance-nick: suggested tweak: make bridge non-refundable and expire to zero value. document GAAP rationale in product playbook.

beth: launch criteria checklist (draft):
- legal sign-off on T&C language
- finance sign-off on recognition model
- eng automation + telemetry implemented
- sales one-pager + console UI
- internal pilot with 10 customers (2 weeks)
- rollback plan if abuse spawns unexpected cost

oleg: add monitoring alerts: >50% bridge consumption in 7 days for a single account -> flag for manual review.

billing-bot: automated note: "Reminder: test account sandbox created: acct-bridge-pilot-01" :robot_face:

julio: customer-facing price examples would help sales. beth can we draft 2 variants: conservative and aggressive?

beth: yes. quick mock:
```
Plan | Commit | Bridge
Starter | $500/mo commit | up to $250 one-time bridge (30d)
Scale | $2k/mo commit | up to $800 one-time bridge (30d)
```
Conservative = smaller caps, aggressive = cap at 100% of trial.

eng-kai: agree run conservative pilot (50% of trial) first. fewer edge cases.

maria: timeline suggestion: PRD end of week, eng spike next week, pilot rollout in 3 weeks.

beth: action items: @eng-kai draft automation design (due in 3 days), @legal-lena draft T&C snippet, @finance-nick confirm accounting approach, @julio assemble 3 pilot customers. I'll own PRD and pilot coordination.

julio: pinged a few customers already. will share list by EOD. :thumbsup:

beth: thanks everyone. if no objections by EOD tomorrow I'll lock the PRD and schedule eng spike.
